statement: When a protocol requires an agent to hold key material in a curve/format the agent's existing custody does not natively produce, the correct construction is a pure, on-demand, deterministic derivation from the agent's EXISTING signing custody — never a second, independently-generated or independently-persisted secret store for the new curve/format. The derivation MUST be re-computable on demand (no requirement to persist its output), and its EXISTENCE must never be conflated with, or substituted for, a constitutional authority/mandate check: proving communication capability (possessing or deriving a valid key) and proving authorization to act are separate planes, and code that derives or accepts the former must never shortcut the latter.

canaries.assertion: Determinism (same agent Ethereum key -> same derived P-521 keypair across independent calls), cross-agent isolation (two different keys -> two unrelated keypairs, no shared module-level state), rejection-sampling correctness (masking rule + retry-loop-advances-on-rejection both exercised directly, not just the end-to-end happy path), key-possession-is-not-authority (a validly derived key composed with `deriveActionAuthorisation()` under no authority still REFUSES; the identical possession under ACTIVE authority authorises — proving the derived key was never itself the gate), and no-new-persistent-store (grep-provable: no database write, no `process.env` read in the derivation module).

occurrences.defect: `VelaClientAdapterOptions.requesterP521PrivateKeyHex` had no in-repo derivation from the agent's existing Ethereum custody; every caller either generated a fresh random P-521 key or hardcoded one, creating a second key-provisioning path outside AgentKeyService's custody chain.

notes: This is the FIRST recorded occurrence — status stays `candidate` per this loop's own discipline ('a lesson does not become doctrine because a fix worked once'); `validated` requires a second recorded occurrence or demonstrated regression prevention, and only an operator act may raise this to `ratified`/`canonical`.

The prior sibling pattern in this same subsystem — `CI-2026-08-22-VELA-APPLICATION-ID-DEPLOYMENT-RECORD-001` ('a Vela applicationId is a deployment record, never a durable identity') — is a different rule about identifier durability, not about custody/derivation; the two are complementary but distinct and this candidate does not supersede or restate it.

Analogous existing precedent this candidate generalises FROM (not derived from, since it predates this loop's own record-keeping): `services/wallet/agentPurposeWalletService.ts` already extends `AgentKeyService`'s AES-256-CBC custody path for purpose-bound wallets rather than inventing a parallel store — the same 'existing custody, not a new secret surface' discipline, applied there to a same-curve purpose-bound key rather than a cross-curve derived one.

Flags, but does not resolve, a separate open question surfaced while implementing this candidate: `services/identity/agentKeyService.ts` (V1, 16 production importers) and `services/identity/agentKeyService.v2.ts` (V2, 1 importer, a debug/test route) coexist with no resolution record explaining the divergence — this candidate's derivation module was built against V1's shape (a raw `evmPrivateKey` hex string) since that is the actively-used surface, but the V1/V2 coexistence itself should get its own resolution record if/when it is addressed, not be silently collapsed as a side effect of unrelated work.
